critical_code_review_comments: uploads.py: PUBLIC_BASE is built from FRONTEND_URL at import time; if FRONTEND_URL is unset, the returned upload url is a relative '/api/files/...' which the frontend still resolves via axios base. Confirm FRONTEND_URL is set for production so the url field is a fully qualified https URL for storefront/product cards and email templates.
uploads.py: 5 MB size limit is enforced only AFTER file.read() into memory; a large upload will still buffer fully. For MVP acceptable, but consider request-size middleware.

notifications.py send_email: exceptions from _assert_safe_email() are raised (not caught) inside send_email; notify_order wraps it in try/except so create-order won't 500, but consider catching inside send_email itself for symmetry with send_sms.

notifications.py notify_order: ObjectId(order['user_id']) can raise InvalidId if a legacy record ever stored a non-ObjectId string; wrap in try/except (currently only bare except catches, which is fine — noted).
delivery.py compute_slots: still N+1 count_documents per slot; iteration_1 note still applies.

Prior iteration_1 finding: brute-force lockout keyed by request.client.host is a no-op behind the ingress proxy. Re-verified this iteration — test_brute_force_lockout in test_backend.py NOW PASSES because pytest-xdist workers hit the same pod IP consistently. In production/manual traffic across pods the lockout will still be bypassable. Recommend trusting X-Forwarded-For (leftmost) or locking by email only.
